description: Every run setting: type, default, allowed values, and a plain-language explanation. Python validates run configs against this file; the MATLAB app builds its controls and tooltips from it. Fields marked advanced are hidden behind 'Advanced settings' in the app.

fields.label: What to learn
fields.help: classify: learn to tell trial conditions apart (for example early vs late learning, or CS+ vs CS-) from the recorded signals. mae (masked autoencoder): learn the structure of the signals by hiding part of each trial and predicting it; needs no labels.

fields.label: Run name
fields.help: Optional short name, added to the run folder's name.

fields.label: Preset
fields.help: quick: a small model that trains in minutes on a laptop, to check that everything works. standard: a larger model for real analyses. paper: the configuration of the PRISMt paper (needs a GPU). custom: your own settings.

fields.label: Dataset file
fields.help: A PRISMT dataset (.mat) written by prismt.writeDataset or the Data tab.

fields.label: Trial filters
fields.help: Keep only trials that match every filter, for example stim is CS+, or response is hit or CR.

fields.label: Channels
fields.help: Names of the channels to use. Empty: all channels.

fields.label: Modalities
fields.help: Names of the modalities (signals) to use, for example calcium and ach. Empty: all.

fields.label: Trials per session (at most)
fields.help: Use at most this many randomly chosen trials from each session, to make a test run faster. Empty: all trials.

fields.label: Minimum data present per trial
fields.help: Skip a trial if less than this fraction of its values are present (not missing).

fields.label: Label column
fields.help: The trial column whose values the model learns to tell apart, for example phase or stim.

fields.label: Classes
fields.help: Which values to compare. Values given the same class name are merged (for example hit and CR as 'correct'). Empty: every value is its own class.

fields.label: Class weighting
fields.help: balanced: rare classes count as much as common ones, so the model cannot score well by always guessing the most common class.

fields.label: Time window (s)
fields.help: Use only samples between these two times, in seconds relative to the event (for example 0 to 3). Empty: the whole trial.

fields.label: Time bin width (s)
fields.help: Average consecutive samples into bins of this width. Fewer time bins make training much faster: the model's cost grows with the square of (time bins x channels). Empty: keep every sample.

fields.label: Subtract pre-event baseline
fields.help: Subtract each trial's average before time 0, channel by channel.

fields.label: Scaling
fields.help: zscore_train: scale each channel to mean 0 and standard deviation 1, computed on training trials only (never on test trials). none: use the values as they are.

fields.label: Clip at (standard deviations)
fields.help: After scaling, limit values to plus or minus this many standard deviations so rare artifacts cannot dominate training. Empty: no limit.

fields.label: Test on
fields.help: What the final score must generalize to. subject: animals never used for training (the strongest claim). session: new sessions of known animals. trial: held-out trials of known sessions, only valid when the label changes within sessions. auto: the strongest level your data allow.

fields.label: Validate on
fields.help: Validation trials decide when to stop training and which epoch to keep. They are held out at this level from the training data. auto: the same level as testing when there are enough groups.

fields.label: Evaluation
fields.help: auto: one train/validation/test split when there are 10 or more groups, otherwise cross-validation so that every animal is tested once. A number k: k-fold cross-validation. loo: leave one group out (each animal is the test set once).

fields.label: Test fraction
fields.help: Fraction of groups used for testing when there is a single split.

fields.label: Validation fraction
fields.help: Fraction of the training groups held out for validation.

fields.label: Split seed
fields.help: Changes which animals end up in training, validation and test. Results should not depend on it much.

fields.label: Allow leaky split
fields.help: Allow the same session or animal in training and testing even though the label is constant within it. Scores will be inflated; for exploration only.

fields.label: Model width
fields.help: Size of the internal representation of each token. Larger models can learn more, but need more data and time.

fields.label: Layers
fields.help: Number of transformer layers. More layers can combine information in more complex ways.

fields.label: Attention heads
fields.help: Number of parallel attention patterns in each layer. Must divide the model width.

fields.label: Feed-forward size (x width)
fields.help: Width of each layer's feed-forward network, as a multiple of the model width.

fields.label: Dropout
fields.help: Randomly drops parts of the network during training to reduce overfitting.

fields.label: Attention
fields.help: block_causal (as in the PRISMt paper): each time bin can use the present and the past, never the future. full: every token can use every other token.

fields.label: Time bins per token
fields.help: 1: one token per value (the paper's model). A larger number groups that many consecutive time bins of a channel into one token: faster, but coarser in time. all: one token per channel.

fields.label: Position encoding
fields.help: channel_time: the model learns one code per channel and one per time bin, and adds them. per_token: one code per (channel, time) token, as in the PRISMt paper; needs more data.

fields.label: Start from autoencoder
fields.help: Start the classifier from a finished masked-autoencoder run on the same dataset (fine-tuning). Give the run folder.

fields.label: Freeze autoencoder
fields.help: When starting from an autoencoder, train only the classification head and keep the rest fixed.

fields.label: What to hide
fields.help: random: hide random tokens. channel: hide whole channels (which channels are predictable from the others?). forecast: hide the end of each trial (predict the future). modality: hide one modality (predict, for example, ACh from calcium).

fields.label: Fraction hidden
fields.help: For random: the fraction of tokens hidden (the PRISMt paper used 0.9). For channel: the fraction of channels hidden.

fields.label: Forecast: fraction of the trial shown
fields.help: For forecast: the first part of the trial that the model sees.

fields.label: Modality to hide
fields.help: For modality: which modality to predict. Empty: a random modality on each trial.

fields.label: Example trials to save
fields.help: Number of test trials whose reconstructions are saved for plotting.

fields.label: Epochs (at most)
fields.help: Maximum number of passes over the training trials. Training stops earlier when the validation score stops improving.

fields.label: Batch size
fields.help: Trials per training step. Larger batches are faster on a GPU but need more memory.

fields.label: Learning rate
fields.help: How large each update step is. Too high: training becomes unstable; too low: it learns slowly.

fields.label: Weight decay
fields.help: Pulls weights towards zero to reduce overfitting.

fields.label: Warm-up fraction
fields.help: Fraction of training during which the learning rate ramps up from zero.

fields.label: Final learning rate (fraction)
fields.help: The learning rate decays to this fraction of its peak by the end of training.

fields.label: Gradient clipping
fields.help: Limits the size of each update to keep training stable. Empty: no limit.

fields.label: Early-stopping patience (epochs)
fields.help: Stop when the validation score has not improved for this many epochs. The best model is kept.

fields.label: Minimum epochs
fields.help: Early stopping cannot end training before this many epochs. Transformers often improve slowly at first, then quickly.

fields.label: Validation score
fields.help: What 'improved' means for early stopping and choosing the best epoch. auto: the validation loss.

fields.label: Training seed
fields.help: Seed for weight initialization, batch order and masking.

fields.label: Device
fields.help: auto: an NVIDIA GPU if there is one, otherwise the Apple GPU, otherwise the CPU.

fields.label: Time limit (minutes)
fields.help: Stop training after this many minutes and keep the best model so far. Empty: no limit.

fields.label: Linear reference model
fields.help: Also fit logistic regression on the same trials, as a simple reference the transformer should match or beat.

fields.label: Shuffled-label repeats
fields.help: Also train this many times with shuffled labels to measure chance level for your data. Slow; best run on a cluster.

fields.label: Runs folder
fields.help: Each run gets its own folder inside this one.

fields.label: Report results by
fields.help: Trial columns to break results down by (subject and session mean the columns marked with those roles).

fields.label: Save trial embeddings
fields.help: Save the model's summary vector of every trial, for plotting how trials are organized.

fields.label: Overwrite run folder
fields.help: Allow reusing an existing run folder name. Off: an existing folder is never overwritten.

fields.label: Settings to try
fields.help: How many combinations of model and training settings automatic tuning tries.

fields.label: Tuning time budget (minutes)
fields.help: Stop trying new settings after this long. Empty: no limit.

fields.label: Epochs per tried setting
fields.help: Maximum epochs for each tried setting. Empty: the Epochs setting.

fields.label: Search space
fields.help: default: learning rate, weight decay, dropout, model size and depth. small: learning rate and dropout only.

fields.label: Final repeats
fields.help: The best settings are retrained this many times with different seeds; the test score is reported as mean and spread.

fields.label: Parallel workers
fields.help: On a cluster: how many jobs search in parallel.

presets.name: quick
presets.label: Quick test
presets.description: Small model, a few minutes on a laptop. Checks that everything works.

presets.name: standard
presets.label: Standard
presets.description: Larger model for real analyses; tens of minutes on a laptop GPU, faster on a cluster.

presets.name: paper
presets.label: Paper
presets.description: The PRISMt paper's configuration (model width 512, 90% masking, batch 128, learning rate 5e-4, up to 200 epochs). Needs a GPU.
